content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 (no action): both queues are predicted well above the 80% target from 15:30 to 17:30 at no extra cost.","why":"Payments and general both had fewer agents on the phones than planned at 15:00 and 15:15 (payments 25 vs 33 and 31 vs 36, general 27 vs 33 and 30 vs 37). Absence doesn't explain it, volume is close to forecast and handle time is below forecast. Even with this gap, the disruption window is predicted at 98.9% service level (payments 99.1%, general 98.7%) with 0.1% abandons. Rest of day is 97.5%. No intervention is needed to meet target. Do ask floor leads whether an unplanned meeting, training session or break overrun pulled agents off the phones in both queues at once.","trade_offs":["P2 (IVR callback on both queues 19:00-20:00) is also free and gives identical predictions, including 97.5% rest of day. It adds a safety net for the last hour but makes no measurable difference today.","P3 (chat deflection of 20% of payment status calls 19:00-20:00) costs INR 108. It lifts the rest-of-day figure from 97.5% to 98.5% but leaves the 15:30-17:30 window unchanged at 98.9%, so the spend isn't justified against target.","Neither alternative takes resource from the other queue, so P0 carries no cross-queue risk."],"watch":"The cause of the staffing gap is unknown. If agent counts keep falling below plan in either queue, or service level starts to slide from general's 86.9% at 15:15, reassess. P2 is the free fallback."}
